interest: Captures 1940 US intelligence profiles of Japanese Army leaders Sumita, Doihara, and Sugiyama after the Tripartite Pact and Indochina entry.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.21/5, cross-indexed under Army Maneuvers) comprises three biographic military intelligence reports (Nos. 10,218, 10,219, and 10,220) prepared on October 15, 1940, by Lieutenant Colonel Harry I. T. Creswell, U.S. Military Attaché in Tokyo, for the War Department General Staff Military Intelligence Division (G-2) and subsequently forwarded to the Department of State. The reports provide detailed chronological career summaries, decorations, and reputational appraisals for three prominent Imperial Japanese Army general officers following recent high-level reassignments: Major General Raishiro Sumita, newly appointed to head the Japanese military inspectorate in French Indochina; Lieutenant General Kenji Doihara, seasoned intelligence operative and China hand appointed to the Supreme Military Council; and General Gen Sugiyama, former War Minister who was elevated to Chief of the Army General Staff. Together, the documents illustrate American intelligence tracking of the leadership cadre steering Japan's military expansion across China and Southeast Asia at a critical turning point preceding the Pacific War.

subfiles.about: A biographical military intelligence report outlining the military career and qualifications of Major General Raishiro Sumita upon his appointment to head the Japanese inspectorate in French Indochina.
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Lieut. Colonel, Acting General Staff, Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Military Attaché report profiles Maj. Gen. Raishiro Sumita, an artillery specialist and former attaché to France, now heading Japan's Indochina inspectorate to cut China's supply lines.
subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 10,218: Major General Raishiro Sumita
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division, War Department General Staff

subfiles.about: A biographical intelligence report detailing the career, intelligence activities, and command history of Lieutenant General Kenji Doihara following his appointment to the Supreme Military Council.
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Lieut. Colonel, Acting General Staff, Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Report profiles Lt. Gen. Kenji Doihara's career as a China intelligence specialist, from the 1931 Mukden Incident to his 1940 appointment to the Supreme Military Council.
subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 10,219: Lieut. General Kenji Doihara
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division, War Department General Staff

subfiles.about: A biographical intelligence report detailing the military career, political posts, and strategic leadership of General Gen Sugiyama upon his appointment as Chief of the Army General Staff.
subfiles.from: Harry I. T. Creswell, Lieut. Colonel, Acting General Staff, Military Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Report traces Gen. Gen Sugiyama's career from the Russo-Japanese War to Chief of the Army General Staff, including his 1936 resignation and wartime command in North China.
subfiles.title: Military Attaché Report No. 10,220: General Gen Sugiyama
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division, War Department General Staff
